title: Streamlined KPI envelope + Prometheus adapter for inference metrics
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create a lightweight, production-ready metrics envelope and a Prometheus/OTel adapter for Redwood inference KPIs. The goal is to standardize emitted KPI names and labels from the serving runtime, control cardinality, and provide an efficient ingestion path for both high-frequency counters (QPS, tokens) and latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) without blowing up Prometheus or downstream storage costs. This ticket covers schema design, an adapter service (OTLP->Prometheus+/Pushgateway), aggregation rules for inference-specific metrics, and dashboards + alert SLI mapping.
background_and_goal: Current metric emission from the runtime includes many high-cardinality labels (request_id, prompt_hash, dynamic client tags) that cause ingestion spikes and slow down the metrics pipeline. We need a standard "KPI envelope" that the runtime will emit (instrumentation spec) with required and optional labels, cardinality caps, and sampling rules. The adapter will collect OTel metrics, apply deterministic aggregation (model_id, model_variant, route, region, shard), downsample or rollup ephemeral labels, and export to Prometheus remote_write and our internal metrics fabric. Ultimately dashboards must show accurate per-model latency curves and token cost breakdowns while keeping series count reasonable.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation spec published in Confluence with label whitelist and naming conventions
Prototype adapter service converts OTLP metrics to Prometheus metrics with configured aggregation rules
End-to-end benchmark: <20% additional ingestion cost vs baseline while preserving p99 latency within 5% of raw values
Grafana dashboards updated with new panel templates for per-model p50/p95/p99 and batch-size distribution
Canary rollout plan + runbook for reverting adapter if metric regressions or cardinality spikes occur
implementation_notes: Design a compact metric name prefix: rw_inference_<metric> e.g., rw_inference_tokens_total
Use label keys: model, model_variant, customer_tier, route, region, batch_size_bucket
Drop or hash high-cardinality labels (client_id -> client_segment, prompt_hash -> prompt_family)
Histograms: use pre-defined exponential buckets tuned to token latency (1-4096ms) and set exemplar support for traces
Counters: aggregate by 1s bins at adapter then emit Prometheus counters using remote_write to avoid pushgateway scaling issues
Sampling: deterministic sampling by request_id modulo N for trace linkage while keeping counts adjusted via weight label
Shard awareness: adapter respects serving shard id and merges consistently using monotonic counters
Backfill migration: dual-write adapter for 2 weeks to compare legacy vs new metrics and compute mapping functions
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: Option A (current): emit fully-labeled metrics from runtime -> high fidelity but unsustainable cardinality/cost
Option B (this ticket): emit compact envelope + adapter -> lower cost, small fidelity loss on rare label combinations
Option C: rely solely on traces for high-cardinality slices and only emit aggregated metrics -> increases dependency on tracing storage and makes SLIs harder to compute in Prometheus
We chose Option B to balance observability and cost and to keep SLIs in metrics layer for alerting
progress_updates: 2026-02-10: Spike complete. Evaluated cardinality patterns using 7 days of prod metrics. Draft spec created.
2026-02-16: Prototype adapter (Go) that accepts OTLP/gRPC and applies label rollups. Microbenchmark shows 3k reqs/s per vCPU.
2026-02-20: Design review with PM and Console team. Agreed on label whitelist and histogram buckets.
2026-02-24: Integration test with staging runtime; observed correct downsampling but p99 error shifted by ~2.8% - within target.
2026-03-01: Security review checklist filled; decided no extra KMS integration required for metrics. Preparing canary plan.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: accidental loss of critical label leading to missed SLI signals. Mitigation: dual-write for 2 weeks and one-off scrub queries on raw metrics before cutover.
Risk: adapter becomes a bottleneck at high QPS. Mitigation: horizontally scale adapter with consistent-hash routing and use batched export to remote_write.
Risk: mismatch between legacy dashboards and new names. Mitigation: provide mapping shim in Grafana and deprecation window + redirect panels.
Risk: increased cardinality from customer tags. Mitigation: server-side enforcement of whitelist and runtime validation errors logged to audit stream.
